text: This very [process] is called the apprehension of the sign. Consequently, the knowledge "the mountain has fire" arises as the inference. This is inference for oneself. However, when one, having inferred fire from smoke for oneself, employs the five-membered syllogism to make another understand, that is inference for others. For example: The mountain has fire, because it has smoke. Whatever has smoke has fire, as in a kitchen. This [mountain] is also such. Therefore, it is so. Through this, by means of the sign established, the other person arrives at the conclusion of fire.
